findings.view: world-reentry-plasma.png (whole frame; panes x 880-1010, y 215-610 and x 1200-1440, y 310-620); reentry-plasma.png (windows x 870-980, y 200-600 and x 1190-1390, y 320-620)
findings.defect: The integrated reentry view is a flat, shadowless, uniformly pink cabin around two black windows: it reads as an unlit albedo pass with a colour filter. Frame mean 138 / 255, the brightest of all 22 screenshots; the blanket bays are one tone (median 198,167,173) with no gradient away from the windows and almost no pillow shading; the gaps between blankets, frames and liner panels are pure black slits (x 440-470, y 0-130; x 580-610, y 430-600; x 0-50, y 240-300); the panes show black space and a blocky blue reflection. The light source is not in the picture. In the lab frame the same windows clip to cream white (15 % of the window crop at 255) under a bloom halo that hides the frames: no hue, no streaks.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/reentry-chutes/eft1-plasma-side-window.jpg: the window shows a pink-magenta to salmon field (mean 120,95,109) crossed by fine streaks with a hot white-yellow core at one edge, still coloured, never a blank white or black pane. Entry footage from inside Orion, Soyuz and Dragon: the glow washes the window frames and the nearest surfaces only, the cabin stays lit by its own white lamps.
findings.likelyCause: The cockpit lights the cabin from snapshot plasmaIntensity (cabin.plasma, 320 cd/m^2) whether or not anything glows outside: the vfx plasma is not drawn for an interior camera (request cockpit-9, open), so the panes transmit black space. The pink reaches the surfaces mostly through the probe bounce (no direction, hence no relief), and the interior meter exposes the evenly pink cabin above mid-grey. In the lab the stand-in window radiance is several stops over the cabin, so the tone curve clips every channel.
findings.fixDirection: Do not ship a lit cabin without its source. Until cockpit-9 lands, draw the shock-layer glow in the cockpit's own glass pass (per-pane emissive term with streak structure and the per-window flicker the cabin light already has), and derive the cabin's plasma light from that same term so pane and cabin cannot disagree. Let the direct window term dominate the tint (bright on the bezels and the nearest blankets, falling off with distance, white flood light elsewhere), hold the pane within about 2 EV of the cabin so it keeps its hue, and re-shoot the integrated frame; assert in world.spec.ts that the pane's mean luminance is above the cabin's when plasmaIntensity > 0.

findings.view: world-pad-noon-forward-window.png and pad-noon-forward-window.png (x 1190-1400, y 725-820); world-night-displays-floods.png / night-displays-floods.png (x 1160-1320, y 160-260); world-leo-sun-patch-console.png (x 1350-1580, y 170-270); reentry-plasma.png (x 1290-1400, y 660-730)
findings.defect: The caution-and-warning matrix is torn into fragments. Instead of a regular grid of rectangular legend lenses the panel shows scattered triangles and pentagons: some cells are missing, others are cut diagonally, the lit green and amber lamps are arrow-shaped or ragged quadrilaterals, the lit white lamp at night is a triangle. Visible from the seat in every view that contains the panel; it will flicker as the head moves.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/cockpit-interiors/apollo11-columbia-panel.jpg: annunciator and legend lamps are identical rectangular caps in a regular grid, each with a complete outline and a complete legend.
findings.likelyCause: Coplanar faces (z-fighting). src/render/cockpit/cabin/console.ts annunciator(): the housing is ctx.b.box(offsetFrame(f,0,0,0.008), ..., 0.008, ...) (line 410): centre 8 mm, half depth 8 mm, front face at 16 mm. Each lens is built on offsetFrame(f, ..., 0.016) (line 414) and lens() draws its box at offset -0.002 with half depth 0.002 (lines 424 and 429): front face at exactly 16 mm, inside the housing's front face (box() in mesh.ts takes half extents about the frame origin). With the depth pre-pass and an 'equal' test, whichever triangle wins per pixel shows.
findings.fixDirection: Stand the lenses proud of the housing (0.5-1 mm) or cut a pocket for each lens in the housing face (the console's part-aware grid can leave the holes), and add a unit test that no two opaque faces of the console are coplanar and overlapping. Then check the lit lamps: a full rectangle with an even glow.

findings.view: hatch-mechanism.png (x 980-1330, y 310-530; arcs on the window ring at x 690-700, y 600-690 and x 990-1000, y 540-620); look-back-couches-hatch.png (x 885-1040, y 232-255)
findings.defect: The seam between the hatch door and its frame still glows: a white strip in four segments (broken only by the latch brackets) with bloom, 1262 pixels at 255 in the crop, against a door at about 40 / 255. It is also visible from the commander's seat in the look-back view as a bright white line behind the couches.
findings.realReference: A plug hatch seats on a continuous seal (Apollo unified hatch, Orion side hatch): the seam is the darkest line on the door, a seal bead in contact shadow.
findings.likelyCause: Not geometry (the fixer's ray test passes) and not one of the three causes the fixer excluded. Two candidates not yet tested: (a) the strip is the polished aluminium seal land (metallic 1, roughness about 0.3) mirroring the probe's clipped hatch-window texels: the probe term in shaders.ts (line 1024) is cut only by cabinSpecOcclusion(), which is derived from the baked AO and cannot know that the door hides the window from the land; (b) the analytic sun term sunThroughWindows() admits points that lie in the plane of the wall next to an opening.
findings.fixDirection: Output material id, sunThroughWindows(p), sunMapVisibility and the probe specular as debug colours at those pixels (the step the hand-off lists as not yet tried). If (a): give recessed lands a bent-normal or horizon test for the probe lookup (or a rough anodised finish), and clamp probe specular by the baked per-window visibility of the reflected direction. If (b): bound the aperture test by the window prism on both its inner and outer loop. Acceptance: no pixel above the door's own luminance along the seam, from the hatch view and from the seat.

findings.view: pad-noon-forward-window.png and world-pad-noon-forward-window.png (x 790-1050, y 185-250; x 560-745, y 375-400; x 1195-1480, y 290-385); look-back-couches-hatch.png (x 0-290, y 60-80; x 130-330, y 380-420; x 150-400, y 620-790)
findings.defect: Thin ragged bright lines trace the rims of the blankets, and the look-back view still has the dotted white sparkles the report calls gone: 147 pixels above 200 and a maximum of 255 in x 120-440, y 580-800, against a blanket at about 44. In the pad views the line wanders like a height contour along the blanket's lower rim above and beside the forward windows (up to 167 against 96 in the world frame, and the brightest thing on the wall in the lab frame). They will crawl in motion.
findings.realReference: Soft goods tucked under a frame flange end in a dark, continuous shadow line (out/qa/ref/cockpit-interiors/soyuz-ms20-descent-module.jpg: every liner edge is darker than the liner).
findings.likelyCause: The line follows a contour of the displaced quilt relief, so it is the intersection of the relief with a plane or a depth, not a hole: most likely the pillow surface rising through the boundary of the analytic sun aperture (the same 'lit inside the slab between the aperture's two ends' fault the fixer found on the wall, src/render/cockpit/shaders.ts cabinSun / sunThroughWindows), or through its own undisplaced caster in the sun map (the relief is not in the map; the skim fade smoothstep(0.03, 0.14, NoL) only removes the most grazing part). The dots in the look-back view may be the satin press studs and slivers of the tie-down rails mirroring a clipped window in the probe.
findings.fixDirection: Debug view first (material id, sunThroughWindows, sunMapVisibility). Then: test the aperture as a prism (the point's projection along the sun must fall inside the opening at both the outer mould line and the inner bezel), render the blankets into the sun map with their displacement or exclude cloth from the direct-sun term within one relief height of its rim, and widen roughness by the pixel footprint for sub-pixel metal parts. Add the magenta-clear test and a test that no interior pixel outside every window prism receives direct sun.

findings.defect: Pixel-scale salt-and-pepper noise covers the blanket and the frame at the lower right of the hatch view: a binary white / dark stipple whose density ramps from a few dots to television static (4.5 % of the region above 180, standard deviation 56 levels), plus a dotted white line on the frame above it and streaked green-white bands on the handhold tube (x 1440-1570, y 760-830).
findings.realReference: A penumbra on cloth is a smooth gradient; there is no grain at any exposure (out/qa/ref/cockpit-interiors/aldrin-lm-interior.jpg: window light on the suit and the panels is smooth).
findings.likelyCause: The cockpit's own sun filter is a fixed 6 x 6 grid and cannot produce stochastic grain (shaders.ts sunMapVisibility, about lines 606-616), so this is either the core's noise-rotated cascade filter reaching interior pixels (the core's sun leaking past the cascade shell near the hatch, the same grain as on the window wells), or a per-pixel pass / fail of the sun map's receiver-plane depth (dzduv) at grazing incidence on displaced cloth. The bands on the tube are the 128^2 probe's texels on a polished cylinder.
findings.fixDirection: Show which term lights those pixels (core sun, cabin sun, probe). If the core's sun: close the shell there or zero the core's direct term for interior material ids. If the cabin's map: clamp dzduv, use a normal-offset bias scaled by 1 / NoL and fade the direct term to zero below the angle where a texel spans more than the relief. Sample the probe at a roughness of at least the texel footprint on small-radius parts.

findings.view: world-leo-sun-patch-console.png (patch x 810-1250, y 310-650); leo-sun-patch-console.png; perf-1440p-leo-seat.png
findings.defect: In the Earth-lit cabin the sun patch is a flat 255 cut-out with a wide bloom halo: 49 % of x 1170-1300, y 330-500 and 5 % of the whole frame are clipped; the black anodised bezel, its keys and the panel are the same white, and the whole flight page of MFD 1 is erased (in the lab's dark cabin the screen stays a readable grey). Dark parts inside the patch do not read darker than light ones.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/cockpit-interiors/aldrin-lm-interior.jpg and apollo7-schirra-inflight.jpg: a sunlit window or patch is over-exposed (Y 0.6-0.7 to clipped) but the surfaces in it keep texture, screw heads and the difference between dark and light paint; the ratio to the shaded cabin is about 22x.
findings.likelyCause: The patch is about 7 stops over the cabin and the core's interior highlight term stops down by 1.25 EV at most (hand-off, known weaknesses); the tone curve has no shoulder left at +5 EV, so albedo 0.03 and 0.2 both land on 255. The display's emissive image is far below the reflected sun and its cover-glass term adds the full sun on top.
findings.fixDirection: Either let the interior meter weigh the patch harder when it fills more than a few per cent of the frame (cabin darker, as in the photographs), or ask the core for a longer highlight shoulder for interior cameras so that +4 to +6 EV still separates albedo 0.03 from 0.2. Check the display under sun separately: a washed-out but legible page, as in closeup-mfd.png.

findings.view: closeup-mfd.png (x 1230-1360, y 130-230; x 1250-1360, y 480-570; x 880-1230, y 40-110); leo-sun-patch-console.png and world-leo-sun-patch-console.png (x 1195-1260, y 365-480)
findings.defect: The combs are gone, but the shadow edges that raised parts cast into the sun patch now end in fans of 6 to 8 stacked, offset copies of the edge: a stepped, banded penumbra several centimetres wide beside a razor-sharp vertical edge of the same shadow. From the seat it reads as a feathered, stair-stepped notch on the right side of the patch.
findings.realReference: Sun through a spacecraft window (Apollo CM, ISS cupola): the shadow of a part 5-20 cm from the receiver has a continuous penumbra of 0.5-2 mm (distance x 0.0093); wider penumbrae are smooth ramps, never steps.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/cockpit/shaders.ts sunMapVisibility(), lines 606-616: after the blocker search the filter is a regular 6 x 6 grid of comparisons with stepUv = pen / 3. When the estimated penumbra (blocker distance x solar diameter, up to SUN_PENUMBRA_MAX, stretched by the grazing incidence) is many texels wide, the six taps per axis are farther apart than a texel and each tap draws its own copy of the edge: six bands. The blocker distance is over-estimated where the bezel's shadow meets the window-edge shadow (a far and a near blocker averaged).
findings.fixDirection: Make the tap spacing never exceed about one texel: raise the tap count with the penumbra width (or use a rotated Poisson disc with at least 32 taps and bilinear comparison, fixed per texel so it stays noise-free), or prefilter the tile (summed-area or mip chain of a variance / moment map) for wide penumbrae. Clamp the penumbra by the nearest blocker, not the mean. Add the 8 / 15 / 30 degree browser test and assert that the lit fraction across an edge is monotonic and has no plateau wider than 2 px.

findings.view: closeup-fdai.png (dome rim x 740-1060, y 195-700); world-leo-sun-patch-console.png (x 660-840, y 390-570); leo-sun-patch-console.png
findings.defect: The new dome glass of the attitude indicator carries torn, hard-edged grey-white fragments all round its rim, with stair-stepped outlines, like chipped paint or shattered glass. In the Earth-lit seat view the instrument is ringed by white flecks.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/cockpit-interiors/apollo11-columbia-panel.jpg: the FDAI's domed glass shows a few smooth, curved highlights of the windows and lamps; reflections stretch continuously toward the rim.
findings.likelyCause: The glass pass samples the cabin probe at roughness cabin.glare.y / 0.14 (shaders.ts lines 1424-1426): nearly the top mip of a 128^2 cube (0.7 degrees per texel). Near the dome's rim the reflected direction sweeps tens of degrees per screen pixel-row, so single probe texels of the clipped sun patch and windows are magnified into polygons.
findings.fixDirection: For curved glass choose the probe mip from the reflection's angular footprint per pixel (derivatives of the reflected direction), not from a constant roughness, and clamp the probe radiance used for glass to a few times the cabin mean (keep the exact display, flood and window polygon hits for the sharp glints). Or render the dome's reflection from a second, sharper cube only when the camera is within 0.5 m.

findings.view: look-back-couches-hatch.png (x 590-730, y 140-330; x 1380-1600, y 150-430; x 1210-1250, y 420-450); world-chase-window-night.png (x 640-740, y 560-660)
findings.defect: The harness straps are flat, untextured beige polygons with no thickness, stitching or weave, and their edges break into triangular notches and shards where they cut through the cushions (z-intersection). They read as paper cut-outs laid on the seats.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/cockpit-interiors/soyuz-ms20-descent-module.jpg and dragon-seats.jpg: webbing has a visible weave and stitched edges, a thickness of 1-2 mm that casts a contact shadow, drapes over the pad with slack and twists, and runs through metal adjusters.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/cockpit/cabin/couches.ts harness(), lines 286-303: each strap is a chain of planar quads (b.strip) between hand-placed points at lift = cushion + 4 mm above the back frame, FLAG_OVERLAY. The pads rebuilt this round (channels, piping, crowned tops) bulge through that plane, and neighbouring quads of one strap are not coplanar, so the pad surface cuts the strap along zig-zag lines.
findings.fixDirection: Lay the straps on the pads: sample the pad surface along the strap path and build a ribbon 1.5 mm proud of it with thickness, rolled edges and a little slack; give it the webbing weave and two stitch rows in the detail layer; add adjusters where straps meet the frame. Add a geometry test that no strap vertex lies below the pad surface.

findings.view: world-pad-noon-forward-window.png (panes x 870-1000, y 285-670 and x 1185-1390, y 395-690)
findings.defect: On the pad both forward windows are filled by a near-white quilted sheet (233-250 / 255) with a regular dot moire, seen through the outer opening: the blanket-lined inside of the launch-escape boost cover, lit as brightly as open sky although it sits a few centimetres from the hull in an enclosed gap. The cabin behind is lit as if the windows saw daylight (frame mean 97, brighter than the LEO seat view). At a glance the cabin's own blanket texture seems to be pasted into the windows; no sky, tower or cloud is visible in the brief's 'on the pad at noon looking up through the forward window' view. The sunlit strip of the well beside it carries the cellular grain of the next finding.
findings.realReference: The Apollo boost protective cover left only the hatch window and one crew window uncovered; the covered windows were dark until tower jettison and the cabin was lit by its floods. out/qa/ref/launch-pad/sls-pad-blue-sky.jpg for what an uncovered window would show (sky Y 0.15-0.33, white structure Y 0.63).
findings.likelyCause: Energy that does not add up between features: the cover's inner lining (src/render/vehicle/materials.ts 'blanket', quilt_n) is shaded by the core's sun on its back side with no self-shadow at this range, and the cockpit's window light (windowRadiance / the probe) treats the forward windows as unobstructed sky. out/screens/vehicle/les-boost-cover-hatch.png shows the cover has a port over the hatch window only.
findings.fixDirection: Decide what the pad view is. Either the cover gets ports over the forward windows (request to vehicle-pad; then the view shows sky and tower), or the covered windows are dark: the cover's inside must be in shadow (two-sided caster in cascade 0, request to vehicle / core) and the cabin's window term must be driven by what each window really sees (a per-window occlusion factor from the vehicle, or the probe sampling the real exterior), leaving the floods and the hatch port to light the cabin. Re-shoot and compare with the hatch-port view.

findings.view: world-moon-horizon.png (window x 470-1140, y 250-750; label x 780-825, y 806-816)
findings.defect: The lunar acceptance view is a black frame: 63 % of the pixels are exactly black, frame mean 8 / 255, the cabin and the window frame are invisible (1 / 255). The ground in the window is dim and blue (median 56,72,92: blue / red 1.64, luminance 70 / 255) while the terrain package's own lunar frames are neutral (123,123,123); stars are visible above a ground the spec's comment calls sunlit; the brightest surfaces are the specular streaks on the well's lower wall (up to 146), brighter than the Moon. The only cabin feature is the placard SIDE LEFT glowing at 229 / 255 under the window.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/cockpit-interiors/aldrin-lm-interior.jpg: lunar daylight through the window is blown out (Y 0.7 to clipped) and the shaded cabin sits at Y 0.03, about 22x darker but full of readable panels. orion-a2-sill-moon.jpg: the Moon is neutral grey with real albedo contrast, the sill a visible warm-grey band, space pure black with no stars at that exposure.
findings.likelyCause: world.spec.ts gives this view no sun (the scene's own): the picture looks like a ground lit by earthshine or a very low sun, exposed long enough for stars, or the interior meter (window share about 15 % of the frame, request cockpit-7) is holding the subject two stops under. The cabin gets no fill from the lit ground through the window at this exposure. The placard is a back-lit label drawn at a fixed luminance regardless of the cabin's state.
findings.fixDirection: Place the sun explicitly for this view (20-40 degrees up, to the side), check the hue of the ground against out/screens/terrain/moon-50m.png, and expose so the ground lands near Y 0.4-0.6 with the frame at Y 0.02-0.04 lit by the ground's bounce (the window term already exists: verify it receives the lunar surface radiance). Dim back-lit placards with the flood / instrument-light state. Assert in the spec that the ground's blue / red ratio is within 10 % of 1 and that fewer than 30 % of the pixels are exactly black.

findings.view: world-chase-window-night.png and world-night-displays-floods.png across three runs of tests/browser/cockpit/world.spec.ts
findings.defect: The night views are bimodal. With the same cockpit commit the lit cabin is either bright (night frame mean 65.2; chase frame mean 14.8, spec passes) or 2.5 stops darker (night frame mean 11.3 with 40 % of the pixels black; chase frame mean 1.0, 86 % black), and in the dark state world-chase-window-night fails its own spec: 'mostly black (0.030)' against minNonBlack 0.05 (my second run, 11:24). The dark state appeared exactly when the integration lab had not loaded terrain (another package mid-edit); the spec still passed 7 of those views, including an Earth view without land and a Moon view without a Moon. Even the passing chase frame is 79.7 % exactly black: no hull silhouette, no stars or Earth night side, the right half of the window cut off by a black edge.
findings.realReference: A lit crewed capsule on the night side (Crew Dragon filmed from the ISS): the windows are the brightest thing in frame, their light spills on the well and the nearby hull, the hull is faintly readable against stars. And a measurement that depends on the cabin's lamps must not change with an unrelated feature.
findings.likelyCause: The cabin's displayed brightness at night is set by the core's interior metering and night key (src/render/core/post/exposure.ts, requests cockpit-5 / 6), which evidently takes a different branch when the body under the vessel is not drawn; in the nominal state the night key does not show at all (see the next finding). world.spec.ts only requires the cockpit to be loaded (line 203) and prints, but does not assert, what else the lab loaded.
findings.fixDirection: In world.spec.ts skip (not pass) a view when the lab's loaded list lacks terrain, ocean, sky or atmosphere, and keep the minNonBlack assertion. Find why the night exposure depends on the terrain feature (log exposureInfo() and the sun-visibility input in both states) and file it against the core if it is the meter. Then re-frame the chase shot so the window is not half hidden, and let the cabin's spill and earthshine give the hull a silhouette.

findings.view: world-night-displays-floods.png / night-displays-floods.png (whole frame); compare pad-noon-forward-window.png
findings.defect: The night view is still an evenly lit beige room: frame mean 65 against 41 for the lab's noon view; the blankets sit at 150-190 / 255 on every wall, there is no pool under a flood and no dark corner, the console throws no shadow on the blankets behind it, no lever, guard, handhold or rod casts anything, and the displays tint nothing. The liner beside the forward window shows soft blotches (x 900-1050, y 100-180) where baked per-vertex visibility is interpolated.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/INDEX.md, cockpit-interiors: in Orion's darkened cabin a display is about 67x its surroundings (orion-a2-flyby-hansen.jpg). A cabin under its own lamps may be bright and even (Soyuz, panel Y 0.63), but even then every strap, handle, box and overhang has a soft contact shadow and the recesses go dark (soyuz-ms20-descent-module.jpg), and a night pass is not displayed brighter than a sunlit noon.
findings.likelyCause: Flood visibility is one baked scalar per vertex and lamp at the rest pose (hand-off: no lamp casts a sharp shadow; shadow maps not built for cost), the probe bounce supplies most of the light, and in the nominal integrated state the core's night key leaves the frame at a daylight key.
findings.fixDirection: Give the two or three dominant floods real visibility: static cube or paraboloid shadow maps rendered once at init and when a control moves (zero per-frame cost), sampled with a wide PCF for the 20 cm tubes; keep the baked channels for the rest. Lower the bounce albedo or the flood count until the far wall is at least 3-4x darker than the wall under a lamp, and verify the night key engages in the integrated scene (target: blankets under Y 0.2, displays the brightest thing in frame).

findings.view: world-night-displays-floods.png / night-displays-floods.png (console left edge x 470-530, y 230-640; blanket bays x 0-480, y 520-900 and x 1050-1600, y 740-900); world-chase-window-night.png (x 640-760, y 330-420)
findings.defect: The displaced blankets pass through hard structure and show their mesh. The pillow beside the console bulges in front of the console's left edge and the FDAI panel, so the panel's straight edge becomes a wavy cut line; at seam crossings the relief breaks into star-shaped flat triangles; along the seams the shading has a regular sawtooth (zip-fastener) pattern and fine parallel rows; the quilt's diamonds change scale by about 3x between neighbouring bays and their lines do not continue across a stringer.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/cockpit-interiors/soyuz-ms20-descent-module.jpg: liners are cut round every fitting and end at it with a bound edge; quilting is a thread row in a smooth groove, the cloth between rows is smooth with a few soft wrinkles; shuttle AFRSI blankets (spacecraft-hardware/shuttle-tail-rpm.jpg) keep one quilt pitch across panels.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/cockpit/cabin/shell.ts and quilt.ts: the relief is added along the wall normal with no clearance test against the console and other fixtures; the blanket grid (about 1-2 cm) is aligned to the bay, not to the diagonal seams, so the seam's crease is resolved by alternating triangles; per-bay quilt coordinates are scaled to the bay instead of metric.
findings.fixDirection: Clamp the displacement against a clearance field of the hard parts (or cut the blanket outline back around the console and bezels with a bound edge). Align the blanket mesh to the quilt (vertices on seams and tufts, edges along the diamond directions) or move the crease into the shared relief function's normal only; use one metric quilt pitch for all bays with seams continuing across stringers.

findings.view: hatch-mechanism.png (door x 640-1000, y 400-560 and x 1000-1300, y 600-760)
findings.defect: The hatch door around its window is covered in wispy, smoke-like light smears that radiate from the window ring, with soft dark fingers between them: the light on a flat door follows the mesh.
findings.realReference: A flat painted door lit by its own window has a smooth falloff and a clean contact shadow under the ring and the linkage.
findings.likelyCause: Per-vertex baked window and flood visibility interpolated over the hatch pocket floor, which is still one ring of long radial quads (hand-off section 7, item 10: not re-meshed).
findings.fixDirection: Re-mesh the door face as the console faces were (regular grid refined around the ring, handle, valve and guides, mounted parts as non-occluding overlays with an explicit contact term), or bake the door's visibility into a small lightmap.

findings.view: world-pad-noon-forward-window.png (well strips x 870-1000, y 285-330 and x 955-1000, y 330-640); world-leo-sun-patch-console.png (x 990-1130, y 20-140); world-reentry-plasma.png (x 900-1000, y 215-300; x 1290-1420, y 320-400); chase-window-sun.png (x 790-900, y 240-300; x 880-990, y 590-625); world-chase-window-sun.png (well right wall x 990-1030, y 230-470)
findings.defect: The walls of the window wells still carry a cellular, worm-like grain wherever the sun reaches them, seen through the glass at arm's length in five views (strongest on the pad and in the LEO seat view, where it reads as frosted glass).
findings.realReference: A window well is smooth painted or anodised metal with a clean shadow edge; from 30 cm it has no grain.
findings.likelyCause: The exterior's well faces under the core's noise-rotated cascade filter (request cockpit-10, open); the cockpit's cure (a liner through the wall) was removed for the brief's geometry criterion.
findings.fixDirection: Push cockpit-10: a noise-free near filter for surfaces within about 1 m of an interior camera, or let the cockpit's analytic aperture term shade the well faces when the camera is inside (the vehicle marks them, the cockpit supplies visibility). Verify in the pad and LEO seat views.

findings.view: world-pad-noon-forward-window.png (close-out panels x 1050-1600, y 0-300; duct x 200-400, y 0-190; cable bundle x 0-520, y 370-560); hatch-mechanism.png (lockers x 0-420, y 0-560); world-reentry-plasma.png
findings.defect: Hard parts are still clean single-tone solids: close-out panels, ring frames, stringers, lockers and the console body are smooth gradients with a row of rivets and no surface breakup, scuff, panel gap or wear visible from the seat; the air duct has a 12-16 sided silhouette, the cable bundle is three fused extrusions with mitred bends and a hexagonal grommet. Beside the now convincing soft goods they read as untextured CGI.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/cockpit-interiors/apollo11-columbia-panel.jpg and soyuz-ms20-descent-module.jpg: painted panels show brush and wear marks, chipped edges, stained fastener heads, stencils and Velcro everywhere; ducts and cables are round, wrapped, tied and sagging.
findings.likelyCause: The detail set is still the 8-layer procedural bake at low contrast (hand-off: none of the 50 USD spent); round parts are built with 12-16 segments regardless of screen size.
findings.fixDirection: Spend the texture budget on painted aluminium, anodise and moulded plastic sets with real mid-frequency breakup, add stencil and placard density to the close-outs and lockers, raise segment counts on parts near the eye (32 or more for the duct, swept splines for cables with lacing ties).

findings.view: closeup-switches.png (x 760-1560, y 260-290 and y 560-585); world-night-displays-floods.png (x 540-960, y 690-870)
findings.defect: The position legends under the switches (OFF, UP, SAFE, NORM) are almost invisible: about 12 / 255 on a panel at 5, while the function legends above are bright; at night the upper legends glow white and the lower ones vanish. The panel face itself is a featureless black with no texture or reflection.
findings.realReference: apollo11-columbia-panel.jpg: every legend, above and below a switch, has the same white engraving and stays readable in dim light.
findings.likelyCause: The lower legends use a dimmer ink / are not back-lit (label colour index and FLAG_BACKLIT in console.ts), and the panel's anodised black has almost no specular response to the probe.
findings.fixDirection: One ink and one back-light level for all nomenclature; give the panel paint a faint sheen and fine texture.

findings.view: closeup-switches.png (x 0-560, y 90-650); world-leo-sun-patch-console.png (left half); moon-horizon.png (seat x 180-370, y 290-600)
findings.defect: Blanket stitching is drawn as a ladder of fat rectangular dashes (about 5 mm blocks in a dark band), which reads as a zip or a railway track at close range; the dark seat fabric shows wavy horizontal moire bands in its weave.
findings.realReference: Quilting thread is a 0.5 mm line of 3-4 mm stitches sunk in a groove; a twill weave has one pitch and no interference bands.
findings.likelyCause: The stitch term in shaders.ts materialDetail (quilt case) uses a wide duty cycle and a dark band; the weave tile aliases against the pixel grid on planar pads (no footprint fade at that frequency).
findings.fixDirection: Thin the stitches to thread width with a lighter thread colour and a narrow groove; fade the weave's contrast with the pixel footprint.

findings.view: world-night-displays-floods.png (panes x 840-1000, y 0-100; MFD 3 x 1385-1500, y 340-500; readouts x 1185-1420, y 590-700); world-reentry-plasma.png (pane reflection x 890-960, y 500-600); world-leo-earth-side-window.png (x 1220-1285, y 430-830)
findings.defect: Reflections in flat glass are smoky smudges with blocky, stair-stepped edges (a blue display reflection of about 6 px blocks, a stepped sliver in the Earth view), not a mirror image; MFD 3's page and the seven-segment digits cannot be read from the seat at 1600 x 900.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/cockpit-interiors/orion-a2-glover-reflections.jpg: reflections on a pane are sharp, doubled images of the cabin.
findings.likelyCause: The 128^2 probe (0.7 degrees per texel, lod1 interior) is the only reflection source for flat panes; the angled third display and the readouts fall under 1 px per stroke.
findings.fixDirection: Planar reflection (or a 512^2 face) for the pane nearest the view axis only; enlarge MFD 3's font tier or turn the display toward the commander.

findings.view: world-leo-earth-side-window.png (frame x 800-1600; sea x 850-950, y 0-80; cloud x 0-210, y 600-860)
findings.defect: The Earth view works, but the window frame is a featureless black mass over 45 % of the frame (0-4 / 255, no rim light) and nothing says glass: no reflection, dust or second pane over the view. Two faults of other packages sit in this acceptance frame: contour-line swirls in the sea's glint and terraced plateaus inside the large cloud.
findings.realReference: ISS and Apollo window photographs: the frame is a dark silhouette with rim light on its inner edge; orion-a2-glover-reflections.jpg shows the cabin faintly mirrored over the Earth.
findings.likelyCause: Exposure for the subject leaves the frame under black; the glass terms (veil, reflection) are scaled to the cabin's luminance and vanish at this exposure. The swirls and terraces belong to the ocean and atmosphere-clouds packages.
findings.fixDirection: Let the bezel's inner edge catch the Earth light (the window term on the bezel chamfer), keep a faint veil on the sunlit part of the pane, and pass the two faults to their owners.
